correctness.rationale: For distinct primes p<q, gcd(pq,phi(pq))>1 iff p divides q-1. Thus E(x)=sum_{p<sqrt(x)} pi(x/p;p,1). Fixed p contribute x/[p(p-1)log x] by the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions. For z<p<=x^(1/3), Brun--Titchmarsh bounds the normalized tail by a constant multiple of sum_{p>z}1/[p(p-1)]; for x^(1/3)<p<sqrt(x), writing q=kp+1 gives O(x^(2/3)). The convergent tail vanishes as z grows, proving the stated asymptotic.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a sharp first-order law, with explicit constant, for the first nontrivial fixed-prime-factor layer of cyclic group orders. It reveals a genuine density reversal between the global population and squarefree semiprimes and supplies a natural baseline for higher fixed-prime-factor layers where obstruction events overlap.
